package_info.package_versions: All IPFS deployments since January 1, 2024 (exact commit/version not specified)
package_info.why_malicious: A developer inserted malicious JavaScript into the Tornado Cash frontend, which covertly exfiltrated users’ private deposit notes to an attacker-controlled server, enabling theft of funds. This was a supply chain attack hidden in a governance proposal, targeting users accessing the app via IPFS gateways.

execution_context.file_location: JavaScript frontend code (likely main app logic, e.g., deposit/withdrawal handler)
required_permissions: access to in-memory deposit notes (private keys)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a user interacts with deposit/withdraw functions, the code reads the user's private deposit note, encodes it, and sends it via HTTPS POST to an attacker-controlled server, enabling secret exfiltration of credentials.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exfiltrates sensitive private deposit notes to an external server, which is unnecessary and dangerous in a privacy-focused application.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Tornado Cash UI code should never transmit private deposit notes or secrets to any third-party server; all sensitive operations should remain client-side.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate telemetry or analytics might send non-sensitive usage data, but never private keys or deposit notes.
key_indicators: Network request to untrusted external domain
Encoding and exfiltration of private deposit notes
Malicious logic hidden in routine function calls

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is merged into the Tornado Cash frontend codebase via a deceptive governance proposal.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is deployed to IPFS gateways.

attack_chain.action: Users access the compromised Tornado Cash UI via IPFS gateways (e.g., ipfs.io, cf-ipfs.com).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes in users' browsers.

attack_chain.action: When users perform deposit or withdrawal actions, the malicious code captures their private deposit notes.
attack_chain.leads_to: Private deposit notes are exfiltrated to the attacker's server.

attack_chain.action: Attacker receives deposit notes and can use them to steal funds from affected users.
attack_chain.leads_to: Theft of user funds and loss of privacy.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code in DeFi UIs that reads private deposit notes or keys and sends them to external servers
Unexpected network requests to non-official domains during sensitive operations (deposit/withdrawal)
Obfuscated or hidden logic in user interaction handlers
file_indicators: Modified JavaScript files in Tornado Cash UI with new network request logic
References to external domains not present in official codebase
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests to attacker-controlled domains (e.g., not tornado.cash or official IPFS gateways)
Outbound traffic containing encoded deposit notes or private keys
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor DeFi frontend code for unauthorized network requests, especially during sensitive operations like deposit or withdrawal. Use static analysis to flag code that accesses deposit notes and transmits them externally. Monitor network traffic from user browsers for suspicious POST requests to non-official domains. Compare deployed frontend code hashes to official releases to detect unauthorized modifications.
